god.d: The one true God, who made everything out of love and is always with us.

trinity.d: One God in three Persons: the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit.

creation.d: Everything God made, from nothing, because he is good.

creator.d: God, who made everything that exists.

angel.d: A spiritual being without a body who serves God and watches over us.

soul.d: The spiritual part of a person that lives forever and cannot be seen.

image-of-god.d: Every person is made like God: able to think, choose and love.

dignity.d: The great worth every person has because God made and loves them.

sin.d: Choosing to do or say something that goes against God’s love and his law.

original-sin.d: The first sin of Adam and Eve, which wounded human nature; Baptism frees us from it.

mortal-sin.d: A serious sin done knowingly and freely that cuts us off from God’s life in us.

venial-sin.d: A less serious sin that hurts our friendship with God but does not break it.

conscience.d: The inner voice of judgment that helps us know right from wrong.

free-will.d: The gift to choose for ourselves, and so to love or not to love.

virtue.d: A good habit that helps us do what is right.

theological-virtues.d: Faith, hope and love: gifts from God that lead us to him.

cardinal-virtues.d: Prudence, justice, fortitude and temperance: the habits that good living “hinges” on.

faith.d: Trusting God and believing what he has shown us.

hope.d: Trusting that God will keep his promises and bring us to heaven.

charity.d: Love: wanting what is good for God and for others, and acting on it.

grace.d: God’s free gift of his own life and help in us.

sanctifying-grace.d: The gift of God’s life in the soul that makes us his friends and heirs of heaven.

revelation.d: God showing himself and his plan to us, in the Bible and in Jesus.

scripture.d: The Bible: God’s word written by people he inspired.

tradition.d: The faith Jesus gave the apostles and the Church hands on in her teaching and worship.

magisterium.d: The Church’s teaching office: the Pope and the bishops united with him.

inspired.d: Written by people whom God moved, so that God is the author of what they wrote.

covenant.d: A sacred promise-bond between God and his people.

prophet.d: Someone God sends to speak his word to his people.

messiah.d: The anointed one God promised to save his people: Jesus.

incarnation.d: God the Son becoming man: Jesus is true God and true man.

redemption.d: Jesus buying us back from sin and death by his cross and Resurrection.

paschal-mystery.d: Jesus’ suffering, death, Resurrection and Ascension, by which he saves us.

resurrection.d: Jesus rising from the dead with his body, never to die again.

ascension.d: Jesus returning to the Father in heaven forty days after Easter.

salvation.d: Being saved from sin and death and given life with God forever.

gospel.d: The Good News of Jesus; also the four books that tell his life.

apostle.d: One of the twelve men Jesus chose and sent to teach in his name.

disciple.d: A follower and learner of Jesus.

parable.d: A short story Jesus told to teach about the kingdom of God.

kingdom-of-god.d: God’s loving rule, which Jesus began and which will be complete in heaven.

miracle.d: A wonderful sign of God’s power that goes beyond nature.

holy-spirit.d: The third Person of the Trinity, who gives life and makes the Church holy.

pentecost.d: The day the Holy Spirit came on the apostles; the Church’s birthday.

church.d: The people God gathers in Christ, who share one faith and one baptism.

body-of-christ.d: The Church, in which Jesus is the head and we are members.

catholic.d: A word meaning “universal”: for everyone, everywhere, with the fullness of the faith.

apostolic.d: Founded on the apostles and led today by their successors, the bishops.

pope.d: The Bishop of Rome, successor of St Peter, who leads the whole Church.

bishop.d: A successor of the apostles who leads the Church in his diocese.

priest.d: A man ordained to serve God’s people, teach, and celebrate the sacraments.

deacon.d: A man ordained to serve through charity, the word and some sacraments.

laity.d: The baptized members of the Church who are not ordained.

parish.d: The local community of Catholics with their own church and priest.

diocese.d: A group of parishes under the care of a bishop.

communion-of-saints.d: The union of all God’s holy people: on earth, in purgatory and in heaven.

saint.d: A holy person who is with God in heaven.

mary.d: The Mother of Jesus and so Mother of God; our mother in faith.

immaculate-conception.d: Mary was kept free from original sin from the first moment of her life.

assumption.d: Mary was taken up body and soul into heaven at the end of her life.

theotokos.d: Mary’s title because her Son Jesus is God.

heaven.d: Life with God forever, in perfect happiness.

hell.d: The state of those who die in mortal sin and freely refuse God’s love.

purgatory.d: A final cleansing of those who die in God’s friendship but need to be made holy.

judgment.d: God’s verdict on each life at death and on the whole world at the end.

eternal-life.d: Life with God that never ends.

sacrament.d: An outward sign Jesus gave that really gives us God’s grace.

baptism.d: The sacrament of new birth that frees us from sin and makes us God’s children.

confirmation.d: The sacrament that seals us with the Holy Spirit and strengthens us.

eucharist.d: The sacrament of Jesus’ Body and Blood, given to us under the appearances of bread and wine.

real-presence.d: Jesus is truly, fully present in the Eucharist: body, blood, soul and divinity.

transubstantiation.d: The change of the whole substance of bread and wine into Christ’s Body and Blood.

mass.d: The Church’s highest prayer, in which Jesus’ sacrifice is made present and we receive him.

sacrifice.d: A gift offered to God; Jesus offered himself once for all on the cross.

reconciliation.d: The sacrament of Confession, in which God forgives our sins through the priest.

contrition.d: Sorrow for sin and a decision not to sin again.

absolution.d: The words by which the priest, in Jesus’ name, forgives sins.

penance.d: A prayer or act that the priest gives to help repair the harm of sin and begin again.

anointing.d: The sacrament that strengthens and heals those who are seriously ill or old.

holy-orders.d: The sacrament by which men are ordained as bishops, priests and deacons.

matrimony.d: The sacrament in which a baptized man and woman make a lifelong covenant of love.

vocation.d: God’s call to each person to love and serve him in a particular way of life.

consecrated-life.d: A life given wholly to God through vows, as in religious sisters and brothers.

holy-day.d: A special feast on which Catholics are bound to go to Mass.

sunday.d: The Lord’s Day, when we remember the Resurrection and rest and worship.

liturgical-year.d: The Church’s year of seasons that retells the life of Christ.

advent.d: The season of preparing for Christmas.

lent.d: The forty days of prayer, fasting and almsgiving before Easter.

easter.d: The feast of Jesus’ Resurrection, the greatest feast of the year.

ordinary-time.d: The green weeks of the year when we follow Jesus’ life and teaching.

commandments.d: The ten laws God gave Moses that show how to love God and neighbor.

beatitudes.d: Jesus’ eight sayings on the path to true happiness.

golden-rule.d: Do to others what you would have them do to you.

natural-law.d: The moral law written in every heart, which reason can discover.

moral-law.d: God’s teaching on how to live well, in the natural law, the Old Law and the New Law.

justice.d: Giving to God and to each person what is due to them.

mercy.d: Love that forgives and helps those who are suffering or in need.

works-of-mercy.d: Acts of love that help others’ bodily and spiritual needs.

common-good.d: The conditions that let everyone in a community flourish.

solidarity.d: Standing with others as one human family and sharing their burdens.

stewardship.d: Taking care of God’s creation and gifts.

chastity.d: Using the gift of sexuality in the right way for one’s state of life.

prayer.d: Raising our minds and hearts to God.

petition.d: Asking God for what we need.

praise.d: Prayer that gives glory to God for who he is.

rosary.d: A prayer of repeated Hail Marys while meditating on the life of Jesus.

lectio-divina.d: Prayerful reading of Scripture: read, reflect, respond, rest.

creed.d: A statement of what the Church believes.

dogma.d: A truth of faith the Church has solemnly defined.

heresy.d: Obstinately denying a truth that must be believed.

schism.d: Breaking away from the unity of the Church.

council.d: A gathering of bishops to settle questions of faith and life.

fathers.d: Early Christian writers whose teaching shaped the Church.

martyr.d: Someone who dies for the faith.

monk.d: A man who lives a life of prayer and work in community, apart from the world.

reformation.d: The 16th-century split that began with Martin Luther and divided Western Christianity.

ecumenism.d: Work for the unity of all Christians.

evangelization.d: Sharing the Good News of Jesus with others.

mission.d: The work Jesus gives the Church: to make disciples of all nations.

social-teaching.d: The Church’s teaching on human dignity, justice and the common good.

sanctity-of-life.d: Every human life is sacred from conception to natural death.

faith-reason.d: Two ways of knowing that work together to find the truth.

typology.d: Seeing how people and events in the Old Testament point forward to Christ.

canon.d: The official list of books that make up the Bible.

old-testament.d: The 46 books of God’s covenant with Israel before Christ.

new-testament.d: The 27 books about Jesus and the early Church.

salvation-history.d: God’s plan unfolding through events from creation to Christ.

exodus.d: God freeing Israel from slavery in Egypt, a sign of our freedom in Christ.

temple.d: The holy place in Jerusalem where Israel offered worship to God.

sabbath.d: The day of rest and worship; for Christians, Sunday.

fasting.d: Eating less in order to pray and turn to God.

almsgiving.d: Giving to the poor out of love.

indulgence.d: The Church’s way of removing the punishment due to sins already forgiven.

pilgrimage.d: A prayerful journey to a holy place.

sacramental.d: A holy sign, such as holy water or a blessing, that helps us prepare for grace.

tabernacle.d: The place in church where the Blessed Sacrament is kept.

vestment.d: The special clothing a priest wears at Mass.

holy-water.d: Blessed water that reminds us of our Baptism.

altar.d: The table of sacrifice at the center of the church.

homily.d: The priest’s or deacon’s talk at Mass that explains the readings.

discernment.d: Prayerfully working out what God is asking of you.

prudence.d: The habit of choosing well how to do good in each situation.

fortitude.d: Courage to do what is good even when it is hard.

temperance.d: Self-control that keeps desires in the right order.

humility.d: Seeing the truth about ourselves before God.

forgiveness.d: Letting go of anger and pardoning someone who hurt us.

obedience.d: Listening to and following those who rightly guide us, as Jesus did.

peace.d: Right relationship with God, others and ourselves.

abortion-teaching.d: The Church teaches that human life must be protected from conception.

marriage-bond.d: The lasting union of husband and wife that only death can end.

annulment.d: A Church declaration that a marriage was never validly formed.

evangelical-counsels.d: Poverty, chastity and obedience, lived by those in consecrated life.

inerrancy.d: The Bible teaches without error the truth God wanted put in it for our salvation.

senses-of-scripture.d: The literal sense and the spiritual senses (allegorical, moral, anagogical).

liturgy-of-hours.d: The Church’s daily prayer of psalms and readings through the day.

blessed-sacrament.d: Jesus present in the consecrated Host.

eschatology.d: Death, judgment, heaven and hell, and Christ’s return.

hypostatic-union.d: The union of divine and human natures in the one Person of Christ.

apologetics.d: Giving reasons for the hope that is in us.
